title: YKI test practice: Finnish reading, listening and writing papers · Glossa
description: Timed practice papers for the Finnish YKI test at the basic, intermediate and advanced levels, with a full Finnish course from A1 to C1. What the intermediate test asks, what Finnish citizenship requires, and what the papers do not cover.

card.title: YKI (Finnish)
card.text: Practice papers at all three levels, including the intermediate test for Finnish citizenship.

heading: Practise for the YKI test in Finnish.
lead: Timed practice papers for the reading, listening and writing subtests of the National Certificates of Language Proficiency, at the basic, intermediate and advanced levels. Behind them is a complete Finnish course from first words to C1, so you can work on whatever the papers show you are missing.
fineprint: The Finnish course is free. The practice papers are part of Premium, €8.99 a month or €69.99 a year. Also available for Russian and Ukrainian speakers.

sections.heading: What the intermediate test asks
sections.intro: YKI is run by the Finnish National Agency for Education (Opetushallitus). You choose a level when you register and take all four subtests at that level on one day; at the intermediate level (keskitaso) the day takes about five hours with breaks.
rows: News, articles, opinion pieces, notices and advertisements, with multiple-choice, true/false and open questions answered in Finnish.
The same task types, with fewer texts. 40 minutes, a time Glossa sets because the board does not publish one.
Interviews, conversations, news and short everyday situations, each played twice, with the same question types.
The same task types, with fewer recordings. 25 minutes.
Three guided texts of different kinds, such as a formal email and an opinion for an online forum.
All three tasks and the full 55 minutes, rated by AI against the published YKI writing criteria.
Tasks recorded in a language studio.
Not included: Glossa cannot assess free speech the way YKI's raters do. The course's conversation practice covers the same everyday situations.
sections.note: Based on the Finnish National Agency for Education's and the University of Jyväskylä's published test descriptions, checked in October 2026. From 2027 the Finnish and Swedish tests are to be taken on a computer at the test centre.

sections.heading: Papers to practise on, and a course to learn from

items.title: Two papers at each level
items.text: Basic (A1–A2), intermediate (B1–B2) and advanced (C1–C2), with original texts and recordings on YKI's topic areas: housing, work, health, services, the environment and society.

items.title: Writing rated against the criteria
items.text: Your three texts are rated by AI against the published YKI writing criteria, with what to improve. It is an estimate, not a rater's grade.

items.title: A full course behind the papers
items.text: 76 modules in eight tiers from A1 to C1, with the cases, consonant gradation, the passive and spoken Finnish explained directly, so a weak spot in a paper has a module to go back to.

items.title: Feedback that says why
items.text: Every answer in the course gets feedback with a reason and a link to the grammar rule. Every Finnish word can be tapped for its forms, meaning and audio.

sections.heading: How the practice papers differ from the real test
items: No grade is given. YKI turns points into levels with its own scale, which Glossa does not know, so a paper shows the share of points only and cannot tell you whether you would reach grade 3.
Reading and listening are shorter than the real subtests, in the same task types.
Recordings can be replayed. In the test you hear each one twice, so play it twice and then answer.
Words can be tapped for their meaning while you practise; the real test allows no dictionary.

items.question: Is Glossa an official YKI preparation course?
items.answer: No. Glossa is not connected with the Finnish National Agency for Education or the University of Jyväskylä. The papers follow their published test descriptions, with original content.

items.question: Which level do I need for citizenship?
items.answer: The intermediate level (keskitaso), with at least grade 3 in one of the pairs above. The Finnish Immigration Service decides on citizenship and sets the other conditions.

items.question: What is free?
items.answer: The whole Finnish course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference and word practice are free. The YKI practice papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.

items.question: I speak Russian or Ukrainian. Is there a course for me?
items.answer: Yes. Finnish for Russian speakers and Finnish for Ukrainian speakers have the same YKI papers, with the instructions and explanations in Russian or Ukrainian.

closing.heading: Start with the course, practise with the papers.
closing.text: Sign in with Google, take the placement test if you already know some Finnish, and open the first module or the YKI papers.
